history.heading: Land of Punt and trading cities
paragraphs: Somalia, on the Horn of Africa, may have been part of the ancient Land of Punt, which traded with Egypt. Its coastal cities, such as Mogadishu, Zeila and Berbera, were major centres of Indian Ocean trade. Islam arrived very early, in the 7th century. The Ajuran Sultanate in the 13th–17th centuries and the Adal Sultanate were powerful states.

history.heading: Colonial division
paragraphs: In the late 19th century the Somali-inhabited lands were divided among Britain (British Somaliland in the north), Italy (Italian Somaliland in the south), France (Djibouti) and Ethiopia (the Ogaden), with a further area in Kenya. Mohammed Abdullah Hassan led a long resistance against the British until 1920.

history.heading: Independence and collapse
paragraphs: British and Italian Somaliland united to form the Somali Republic on 1 July 1960. Mohamed Siad Barre seized power in 1969 and established a socialist dictatorship. A war with Ethiopia over the Ogaden in 1977–78 ended in defeat.

Siad Barre was overthrown in 1991, and the state collapsed into civil war among clan-based militias. A famine in 1992 killed hundreds of thousands; a US-led UN intervention ended after the 1993 "Black Hawk Down" battle. Somaliland in the north declared independence in 1991, and Puntland became autonomous. From 2006 the militant group al-Shabaab emerged; an African Union mission has supported the government since 2007. A federal government was formed in 2012.

culture.heading: Nation of poets
paragraphs: Somalis share a common language, Somali, and religion, Sunni Islam, but society is organised around clans. Somali and Arabic are official. Somalia is known as a "nation of poets" with a rich oral tradition.

Pastoralism, especially camel herding, is central to Somali life and identity; Somalia has the world's largest camel population. Food includes canjeero (flatbread), rice with goat or camel meat, and spiced tea. A large diaspora lives in Kenya, Europe and North America.

politics.heading: Federal state
paragraphs: Somalia is a federal parliamentary republic of member states such as Puntland, Jubaland and others. The government in Mogadishu, supported by African Union forces, fights al-Shabaab, which controls parts of the south and centre. Relations between the federal government and member states are often tense.

Somaliland in the northwest functions as a de facto independent state with its own elections but is not internationally recognised; Somalia rejects its secession. Plans to move to direct universal elections are controversial.

economy.heading: Livestock and remittances
paragraphs: The economy is largely informal. Livestock exports, mainly to the Gulf, are the main source of income, alongside remittances from the diaspora, which are very large relative to GDP. Mobile money is widely used. Somalia received major debt relief in 2023.
Recurring droughts and floods cause humanitarian crises. The currency is the Somali shilling, though US dollars are widely used.
